record.paper_title: Around the Gauss circle problem: Hardy's conjecture and the distribution of lattice points near circles
record.original_question: Fix an angle θ and a shift parameter r in the tilted-and-shifted semi-infinite rectangle model R_{r,θ}. If one orders the lattice points of Z^2 ∩ R_{r,θ} by projection onto the long side of the rectangle and then projects them onto the short side, can one prove equidistribution of those short-side projections in [-1/√2, 1/√2] without averaging over the index ℓ, while instead exploiting averaging over r? The paper identifies establishing exactly this stronger equidistribution statement as the major challenge toward proving the vanishing-correlation conjecture.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\theta \in [0, 2\pi)$ be a fixed angle and let $r \in \mathbb{R}$ be a shift parameter. Consider the tilted-and-shifted semi-infinite rectangle
$$R_{r,\theta} = \{(x,y) \in \mathbb{R}^2 : (x,y) = r\,(\cos\theta, \sin\theta) + s\,(\cos\theta, \sin\theta) + t\,(-\sin\theta, \cos\theta),\ s \geq 0,\ t \in [-\tfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}, \tfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}]\},$$
i.e. an infinite strip of width $\sqrt{2}$ along the direction $(\cos\theta,\sin\theta)$, starting at the offset $r$ along that direction. Enumerate the lattice points $\kappa_1, \kappa_2, \kappa_3, \dots$ of $\mathbb{Z}^2 \cap R_{r,\theta}$ in increasing order of their projection $\langle \kappa_\ell, (\cos\theta,\sin\theta)\rangle$ onto the long side of the rectangle. Let
$$p_\ell(r,\theta) = \langle \kappa_\ell, (-\sin\theta, \cos\theta)\rangle \in I := [-\tfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}, \tfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}]$$
denote the projection of $\kappa_\ell$ onto the short side.

It is known that for a set of $\theta$ of full measure (those whose direction is badly approximable by rationals), the sequence $\{p_\ell(r,\theta)\}_{\ell}$ is equidistributed in $I$ on average over $\ell$.

Problem. For generic $\theta$, prove (or disprove) equidistribution of $p_\ell(r,\theta)$ in $I$ without averaging over the index $\ell$, by instead exploiting averaging over the shift parameter $r$. Concretely: show that for almost every $\theta$, there exists a set of shifts $r$ of full density along which, for each fixed $\ell$, the values $p_\ell(r,\theta)$ become equidistributed in $I$ as $r$ varies.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is identified as the major remaining challenge toward proving the associated vanishing-correlation conjecture in the work on Hardy's conjecture and the distribution of lattice points near circles (published in the Journal of the London Mathematical Society, 2024). The equidistribution on average over the index is established, but the stronger statement using averaging over the shift parameter remains open; no subsequent resolution was found.

status_evidence.title: Around the Gauss circle problem: Hardy's conjecture and the distribution of lattice points near circles - Journal of the London Mathematical Society
status_evidence.snippet: Published 2024; establishes equidistribution of projections in tilted rectangles on average over the index for generic angles.
status_evidence.claim: The averaged equidistribution is proved; the non-averaged version exploiting r-averaging is identified as the major open challenge.

status_evidence.title: Around the Gauss Circle Problem (arXiv:2305.03549)
status_evidence.snippet: Projections of lattice points in tilted rectangles, ordered by projection onto the long side, are equidistributed on average for generic angles.
status_evidence.claim: Equidistribution without averaging over ℓ, using averaging over r, is stated as the major challenge.
